newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: TENNIS-VACEK UPSETS IVANISEVIC TO REACH FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-VACEK UPSETS IVANISEVIC TO REACH FINAL.

text.p: Unseeded Czech Daniel Vacek upset top seed Goran Ivanisevic in three sets on Saturday to set up a clash with Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek in the final of the World Indoor tournament.
Vacek, 26, served strongly and returned well to beat the defending champion 6-4 1-6 7-6, while Krajicek beat third seed Thomas Enqvist of Sweden 6-7 6-3 6-4 in the other semifinal.
Vacek, who lost to Ivanisevic in the quarter-finals last week in Milan, broke the Croat's service in the opening game of the match to take the first set 6-4.
In the second set Ivanisevic, who has successfully defended titles in Milan and Zagreb this year, broke Vacek twice to take the match into a deciding third set.
In the final set both players held serve, but Vacek kept his cool in the tie-break, winning 7-2 to clinch the match.
"All the credit to Vacek, his service was good and he read my service well," said Ivanisevic. "My service did not go the way I wanted, I was not feeling the ball."
Ivanisevic, who hammered 1,477 aces last year, only managed 11 against Vacek and hit 11 double-faults. Vacek hit 15 aces and six double-faults.
Krajicek, winner of the tournament in 1995, blasted 23 aces, bringing his tournament total to 83, and lost only 19 points on his own service against Enqvist.
Four of those points he lost during the first set tie-break which he contrived to lose 7-5 after building a 4-1 lead.
"I think it was lack of concentration after getting 4-1 ahead so easy," said the Dutch second seed.
Krajicek broke Enqvist in the sixth game of the second set and seventh game of the deciding set, after the Swede had double-faulted twice, to earn his place in Sunday's final.
